settings.scanLegacyDesc: Walks the entire storage directory and registers any image files not yet in the database. For each new file the patient ID is inferred from the folder name (e.g. {storageRoot}/42/2024-03-15/photo.jpg → patient 42, date 2024-03-15). Images whose folder does not match a known patient are marked as Unassigned and can be linked manually from the Gallery. Files already in the database are skipped. Use this after manually copying images into the storage folder or after restoring a backup.

manual.title: Instruction Manual
manual.subtitle: Complete guide to using Max7 Vista

overview.heading: What is Max7 Vista?
overview.body: Max7 Vista is a clinical patient image management system designed for healthcare professionals. It enables secure capture, organization, and editing of patient photographs and medical images, with support for multiple organizations (tenants), role-based access control, and multilingual operation.

gettingStarted.heading: Getting Started
gettingStarted.body: After logging in, you will see the main navigation sidebar on the left. Use it to navigate between Patients, Capture, Gallery, Settings, and this Manual. Your role (User, Admin, or Super Admin) determines which features are accessible.

patients.heading: Managing Patients
patients.body: Navigate to the Patients section to create, search, edit, or delete patient records. Each patient has a name, patient code, optional date of birth, and notes. Click a patient card to view their full profile and image gallery.

capture.heading: Capturing Images
capture.body: Use the Capture page to take photos directly from your webcam or upload existing files. Select the patient before saving. After capture, you will be taken directly to the Image Editor to annotate and review.

gallery.heading: Gallery & Grid Views
gallery.body: The Gallery shows all images across all patients or filtered by a specific patient. Use the grid selector to display 1, 2, 4, or 8 images per row. Click any image to open it in the editor.

editor.heading: Image Editing
editor.body: The Image Editor provides tools for cropping, zooming, rotating, freehand drawing, and erasing. Use the Arrow tool to draw directional arrows highlighting clinical structures. Use the Circle tool to draw circles marking areas of interest. Add text labels anywhere on the image — multiple annotations of any type are supported. Switch to the Pointer tool to click and drag any text label to reposition it. Use the colour picker to change annotation colour. When done, click Save to persist all edits to disk.

bulkImport.heading: Bulk Image Import
bulkImport.body: The Bulk Import page lets you migrate an existing image archive into Max7 Vista in one step. Two modes are available. Upload ZIP: pack your images into a ZIP file and upload it from any device. Server Folder: on the LAN or desktop version, enter the full server path to the folder containing your images (e.g. /data/photos) and the server reads them directly — no ZIP required. In both modes, the immediate subfolders must be named with the patient ID (e.g. 2116/, 2117/). A single root wrapper folder is detected and skipped automatically. Optionally attach a CSV file with columns id, name, and dateOfBirth to populate patient details; without a CSV, patients are created using the folder name as both ID and name. Capture dates are read from EXIF metadata, falling back to the file modification timestamp. After import, a summary shows patients created, patients matched, images imported, and any files skipped with reasons. Re-importing with a corrected CSV will update the name and date of birth on existing patients without creating duplicates.

documents.heading: Patient Documents
documents.body: Every patient record includes a Documents section where you can store any type of file — Word documents, PDFs, Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, images, videos, and audio files. Click the Upload button or drag-and-drop files directly onto the panel to attach them. To read a document without downloading it, click the eye icon: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files open inside the Microsoft Office Online viewer; PDFs open in the browser's built-in PDF reader; images display inline; video and audio files play with standard media controls. The download button is always available on every file. All documents are stored in persistent cloud storage and remain accessible across sessions and deployments.

settings.heading: Settings & Storage
settings.body: Configure the root storage directory for patient images. In the desktop (Electron) version, a folder browser is available. The Directory Indexing section lets you scan the storage folder to register images that are on disk but not yet in the database — useful after manually copying files or restoring a backup. The scan infers the patient from the folder structure ({patientId}/{date}/image.jpg). Images that cannot be matched to a patient are marked Unassigned and can be linked manually from the Gallery. Files already in the database are skipped.

roles.heading: User Roles
roles.body: Max7 Vista supports three roles: User (can view and capture images), Admin (can manage patients, users, and settings within their organization), and Super Admin (full system access across all tenants).

tenants.heading: Multi-Tenant Setup
tenants.body: Each organization using Max7 Vista operates as an independent tenant. Data is fully isolated between tenants. Super Admins can create and manage tenants, while Admins manage their own organization's data and users.

bulkImport.title: Bulk Import
bulkImport.subtitle: Import an existing image archive into the system in one step.
bulkImport.zipStep1Body: Pack your image folder into a ZIP. The top-level subfolders must be named with the patient ID (e.g. 2116/photo1.jpg). A single root wrapper folder is detected and skipped automatically (e.g. foto/2116/photo1.jpg works too).
bulkImport.zipStep2Body: A spreadsheet with at least an id column matching the folder names. Optional columns: name, dateOfBirth. Without a CSV, patients are created using the folder name as both ID and name.
bulkImport.zipStep3Body: Capture dates are read from EXIF metadata (DateTimeOriginal), falling back to the ZIP modification timestamp. The filename (without extension) becomes the image legend.
bulkImport.selectFilesDesc: ZIP archive is required; CSV is optional.
bulkImport.hintZipInput: Root → Patient ID folder → image files
bulkImport.folderNoZipBody: Enter the full path to a folder that already exists on the server. The server reads the images directly from disk without any upload.
bulkImport.folderStructureBody: The immediate subfolders of the path you enter must be named with the patient ID (e.g. /data/photos/2116/). A single root wrapper folder is detected and skipped automatically (e.g. /data/photos/foto/2116/ also works).
bulkImport.folderCsvBody: Provide a CSV with id, name, and optionally dateOfBirth columns to populate patient records. Without a CSV, patients are created using the folder name as both ID and name.
bulkImport.folderOriginalsBody: Images are copied into the Max7 Vista storage directory. Your source folder is never modified.
bulkImport.configureDesc: Enter the server folder path. The CSV is optional.
bulkImport.folderPathHint: This path must be accessible by the Max7 Vista server process.

migration.title: Migration
migration.description: Move all data (patients, images, users, settings) between the LAN desktop app and the web version. Export from the source system, then import on the destination.
migration.exportDesc: Downloads a ZIP archive containing all patients, images (files included), users, and settings. Use this on the LAN desktop app before switching to the web version.
migration.importDesc: Upload a migration archive exported from another Max7 Vista instance. Existing patients and users are skipped (no duplicates).
